title: Permutations II
statement: Return the unique permutations of `nums`, which may contain duplicates. Sort the result.
hints: Sort first so equal values are neighbors.
Skip a value when it equals the previous value and the previous value has not been used at this depth.
The used array is what distinguishes 'this duplicate was already chosen as the previous sibling' from 'this duplicate extends a deeper position'.

approaches.name: Sorted skip
approaches.explanation: Prune duplicate branches before they run.

editorial: After sorting, a duplicate value may be chosen at a depth only if the identical previous value was also chosen in this permutation. The condition `i > 0 and nums[i] == nums[i - 1] and not used[i - 1]` detects the illegal sibling branch and skips it.
reference_solution:
from typing import Dict, List, Optional, Tuple
from collections import Counter, OrderedDict, defaultdict, deque
import heapq

def permute_unique(nums: list[int]) -> list[list[int]]:
    nums = sorted(nums)
    out: list[list[int]] = []
    path: list[int] = []
    used = [False] * len(nums)

    def dfs() -> None:
        if len(path) == len(nums):
            out.append(path[:])
            return
        for i, value in enumerate(nums):
            if used[i] or (i and nums[i] == nums[i - 1] and not used[i - 1]):
                continue
            used[i] = True
            path.append(value)
            dfs()
            path.pop()
            used[i] = False

    dfs()
    return out
